mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes ML 500 or 63 AMG engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M113 engine for the ML 500 costs £3,200-£4,500 supply-only; a rebuilt M273 costs £4,000-£5,500; a rebuilt M156 for the ML 63 AMG costs £5,500-£8,500; a rebuilt M157 costs £6,500-£10,000 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,000-£2,000 depending on complexity - V8 work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of M156 camshaft adjuster failure on a Mercedes ML 63 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: A pronounced rattling noise on cold starts is the classic warning sign on the M156 engine. This issue can appear as early as 40,000 miles. If ignored, it can lead to poor engine performance and potentially severe damage.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes ML 63 AMG engine (M156) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M156 is one of AMG's most celebrated engines - a naturally aspirated 6.2-litre V8 with exceptional character. While there are no major reported reliability problems, the camshaft adjusters can develop wear. With proper maintenance, these engines are fundamentally strong.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes ML 500 and 63 AMG V8 engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M113 and M273 V8 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles. The M156 and M157 are too new for definitive long-term data, but with proper maintenance, 100,000-150,000 miles is achievable.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes ML 500 or 63 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the M Class is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M113 costs £3,200-£4,500 - comparable to the value of a £3,000-£8,000 vehicle. For the ML 63 AMG, the higher value (£15,000-£40,000) makes replacement even more financially justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes ML 500 or 63 AMG V8 need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 high-performance oil - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. All M Class V8s require approximately 8.0-9.5 litres depending on the engine.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz M Class 500/63 AMG - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The ML 500 launched with the W163 generation in 1998, powered by the M113 5.0-litre naturally aspirated V8 - a robust, torquey engine that established the M Class as a genuine luxury SUV contender. The ML 55 AMG followed in 1999 with the supercharged M113K 5.4-litre V8, marking the beginning of AMG's involvement in the M Class. In 2006, the W164 ML 63 AMG arrived with the M156 6.2-litre naturally aspirated V8 - one of AMG's most celebrated engines. The W166 generation brought twin-turbo technology with the M157 5.5-litre biturbo V8, delivering even more power and torque.

milestones.description: M156.982, 6.2L naturally aspirated V8, 510hp (ML 63 AMG, W164)

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz M Class 500 and 63 AMG is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from M113 timing chain guides to M156 camshaft adjuster wear and M157 turbocharger issues.

items.commonFailure: Timing chain guide degradation - the plastic guides can become brittle with age and heat cycling. Higher-mileage M113 engines will make timing chain noise at start-up. Valve cover gaskets, camshaft solenoid cover gaskets, and oil filter housing gaskets are also common leak points. Typical failure mileage: 40,000-90,000 miles.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz M Class 500/63 AMG Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The M Class 500 and 63 AMG's V8 engines represent the pinnacle of Mercedes performance engineering - from the robust M113 to the celebrated M156 and the twin-turbo M157. However, each has well-documented weaknesses that can lead to significant repair costs. The M113 suffers from timing chain guide degradation, the M156 is prone to camshaft adjuster wear, and the M157 can develop turbocharger bearing issues. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M113 Timing Chain Guide Degradation - The 5.0 V8's Age-Related Failure
problems.rootCause: The M113's plastic timing chain guides can become brittle with age and heat cycling. Higher-mileage M113 engines will make timing chain noise at start-up. The chain tensioner is also a common failure point. Replacing the chain and tensioner is not a bad job but requires specialist knowledge.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 1998-2005 ML 500 is worth approximately £3,000-£8,000 depending on condition and mileage. These classic SUVs sit in a value band where repair decisions require careful consideration - a full engine replacement may approach or exceed the vehicle's value for higher-mileage examples.
problems.recommendation: If your ML 500 exhibits timing chain rattle on cold start, have a specialist inspect the timing components immediately. The M113's timing chain guides are a known weakness with age. On an ML 500 worth £3,000-£8,000, preventative attention to this issue is always the better investment.

problems.h4: M156 Camshaft Adjuster Wear - The 6.2 AMG's Cold-Start Rattle
problems.rootCause: The M156's camshaft adjusters can wear internally, causing a pronounced rattling noise on cold starts. The problem can be traced to the choice of a softer alloy for the plates. This issue can appear as early as 40,000 miles and certainly by 90,000 miles. The official position from Mercedes dealers is to replace the affected camshaft adjusters - typically all four, as they have similar age and wear.
